To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) computation codes can be used to achieve function decoding in DSC, (ii) computation codes can enable end-to-end communication in networks, (iii) computation codes can also be used to achieve message recovery in DSC, and (iv) computation codes cannot enable message recovery in MAC.

(a) a good computation code can be used for full message decoding if the MAC is sufficiently strong, and (b) a good computation (or function) code can be used to achieve the same rate for DSC as a full message code, if the MAC is not too strong.

(1) for any DSC computation code, there is a DSC problem where it does not perform as a good computation code, and (2) for any computation code, there are MACs where it does not enable full message decoding, and MACs where it enables full message decoding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following fundamental questions: What is the relationship between computation codes and communication codes for multiple-access channels?
the duality of communication and computation codes, which are designed to achieve different goals.
a fundamental question in network information theory: what are the fundamental limits of communication versus computation in network information theory?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
computation and communication are duals of each other, but not necessarily for the same codes.
computation codes can be used to enable full message decoding only when the MAC is sufficiently strong.
computation codes are useful for function recovery, but not for full message recovery, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
communication and computation are not dual in a strong sense.
the duality between communication and computation is not perfect.
computation codes are not good communication codes, and communication codes are not necessarily good computation codes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same code can be a good computation encoder for a DSC problem and a good communication encoder for a MAC, but not necessarily for the same MAC.
, in contrast to DSC and compute–forward, computation codes are not a good tool for MACs.
the same codes that are good for computing a function of multiple messages are also simultaneously bad for recovering the messages themselves.
